Boeing 777X: United States. The Boeing 777X is an American long-range, wide-body, twin-engine airliner built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes, undergoing flight testing.
Who is credited with discovering Telescopium?
Telescopium: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is a Latinized form of the Greek word for telescope.
Who is credited with discovering Spontaneous generation?
Spontaneous generation: Anaximander. It was hypothesized that certain forms, such as fleas, could arise from inanimate matter such as dust, or that maggots could arise from dead flesh.
Who is credited with discovering SN 1987A?
SN 1987A: Ian Shelton. SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
This Onmyōdō master advised Heian emperors on astrology and spiritual matters; a Kyoto shrine and an Osaka train station now honor him — who is he?
Abe no Seimei (February 21, 921 AD - October 31, 1005) was a Japanese onmyji, a court official and specialist of Onmyd, during the middle of the Heian period.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Nicknamed 'the heart of the scorpion,' this distinctly reddish variable star is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius — what is it?
Antares is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpius. It has the Bayer designation α Scorpii, which is Latinised to Alpha Scorpii.

Named for the Ancient Greek word for 'star' after its flower shape, this group of roughly 170 mostly Eurasian perennial plants is also known for its late-blooming 'Michaelmas daisies' — which plant group?
Aster (genus) is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who was he?

Bernie Madoff (April 29, 1938 - April 14, 2021) was an American financier, con artist, and stock broker who was the admitted mastermind of the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion.
This family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, sheep, and goats across 143 living species — name the family?
Bovidae is the biological family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals that includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, and goat-antelopes such as sheep and goats.
Sole living family in the mammalian suborder Tylopoda, which group unites camels with llamas and their South American relatives?
Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.

This naturally occurring but largely inactive steroid hormone shields organs like the kidneys from active cortisol, and gets converted back into cortisol by an enzyme mainly in the liver — what hormone is it?
Cortisone is a naturally occurring, mostly inactive pregnene (21-carbon) steroid hormone.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
This soil-dwelling invertebrate of the phylum Annelida is also known by slang names like 'dew-worm,' 'rainworm,' and 'nightcrawler.' What creature is it?
Earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida.

A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime for the United States, this social psychologist and psychoanalyst co-founded a New York psychiatric institute and was associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory — who is he?
Erich Fromm (March 23, 1900 - March 18, 1980) was a German-American social psychologist, psychoanalyst, sociologist, humanistic philosopher, and democratic socialist.
Bred in Brazil as a guard dog, cattle herder, and big-game hunter, this large mastiff-type breed was also once used to catch runaway slaves — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can contain up to 6% caffeine — roughly double the concentration found in green coffee beans — and flavor a popular Brazilian soft drink. Name the plant?
Guarana (from the Portuguese guaran; Paullinia cupana, syns.

This colorless, nearly odorless organic compound is a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms, widely used as a cheap, largely unreactive solvent and found in small amounts in modern gasoline blends — what is it?
Hexane is an organic compound, a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms and the molecular formula C6H14.
This medical condition occurs when the body, or a region of it, is deprived of adequate oxygen at the tissue level — what is it called?

Hypoxia (medicine) is a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of an adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxia may be classified as either generalized, affecting the whole body, or local, affecting a region of the body.

This English mathematician made foundational contributions to matrix and invariant theory, founded the American Journal of Mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and was teaching at Oxford when he died. Who was he?
James Joseph Sylvester (3 September 1814 - 15 March 1897) was an English mathematician.

The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, this astronaut and aerospace engineer first studied in India before earning advanced degrees in the US and flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 — who was she?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 - February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
This small Arctic rodent is a key prey source for tundra carnivores and is the subject of a persistent myth that it marches off cliffs in mass suicide — what animal is it?
Lemming is a small rodent, usually found in or near the Arctic in tundra biomes.
Named for a Dutch physicist, this six-parameter family of linear equations converts spacetime coordinates between reference frames moving at constant relative velocity — what is it?
Lorentz transformation are a six-parameter family of linear transformations from a coordinate frame in spacetime to another frame that moves at a constant velocity relative to the former.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.

This American theoretical physicist and science communicator, a professor at the City College of New York, won a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for a famous science-fiction author, honoring his work bridging science and sci-fi. Who is he?
Michio Kaku (born January 24, 1947) is an American theoretical physicist, science communicator, futurologist, and writer of popular science.
Scholars can't even agree on which elements define it, yet it appears in every human society as a vehicle for creativity through composition and performance — what is it?
Music is the arrangement of sound to create some combination of form, harmony, melody, rhythm, or otherwise expressive content.
A highly corrosive mineral compound with the formula HNO3, this strong inorganic acid is colorless but yellows over time as it decomposes. What is this acid?
Nitric acid is an inorganic compound with the formula HNO3. The compound is colorless, but samples tend to acquire a yellow cast over time due to decomposition into oxides of nitrogen.
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.
Brought on by too little niacin, this disease announces itself with the 'three D's' — dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea, and dementia — what is it?
Pellagra is a disease caused by a lack of the vitamin niacin (vitamin B3).
Which condition, more common in people with obesity or a family history, involves hair and skin debris being drawn into tissue through tiny skin openings called pits?
Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.

This corticosteroid drug treats a huge range of conditions — from rheumatoid arthritis and asthma to eye inflammation and certain cancers — and can be taken orally, injected, or applied to the skin. What is it?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid, a steroid hormone used to treat certain types of allergies, inflammatory conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancers, electrolyte imbalances, and skin conditions.
This root vegetable in the mustard family, whose entire plant (leaves included) is edible, was domesticated in Asia and is now grown worldwide — what vegetable is it?
Radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These pinnipeds, distinguished from true seals by their external ear flaps and ability to walk on all fours, belong to the eared-seal family alongside fur seals, with six living species worldwide. What animal is this?
Sea lion are pinnipeds characterized by external ear flaps, long foreflippers, the ability to walk on all fours, short and thick hair, and a big chest and belly.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
A Canadian cognitive psychologist at Harvard who champions evolutionary psychology and the computational theory of mind, which popular-science author wrote on how children learn irregular verb forms?
Steven Pinker (born September 18, 1954) is a Canadian cognitive psychologist, psycholinguist, popular science author, and public intellectual.
This protective cap of repetitive nucleotide sequences guards the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes from progressive degradation — what is it called?
Telomere (from Ancient Greek (tlos) 'end' and (mros) 'part') is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes (see Sequences).
Divided into the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, this core section of the body is where the head, neck, and all four limbs attach — which body part?
Torso is the central part, or the core, of the body of many animals (including human beings), from which the head, neck, limbs, tail and other appendages extend.
Measuring under five feet long, this critically endangered porpoise is endemic to a small corner of Mexico's Baja California coast — which species?
Vaquita (v-; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.
Inspired by the code-breaking game Mastermind, this once-a-day puzzle gives you six tries and colored tiles to crack the same word everyone else is solving — which game?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Wordle is a web-based word game created and developed by the Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
Comprising over 22,000 species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches, this phylum of segmented worms use parapodia to move — what is it?
Annelid: Phylum of segmented worms. The basic annelid form consists of multiple segments called metameres.

Known only from fragmentary remains including vertebrae and a giant femur first found by a farmer in 1987, this titanosaur may be the largest land animal ever discovered, stretching up to 35 meters — which genus?
Argentinosaurus: Late Cretaceous giant sauropod dinosaur genus.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.
This medical term for blood escaping the circulatory system describes a healthy person as able to lose 10 to 15 percent of their total volume without serious harm — what is it called?
Bleeding: Blood escaping from the circulatory system. Bleeding, hemorrhage, haemorrhage or blood loss, is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.
Typically about two-thirds copper and one-third zinc, which prehistoric substitutional alloy differs from bronze, which swaps in tin instead of zinc?
Brass: Alloy of copper and zinc. Brass has long been popular for its bright, golden appearance and is used for drawer pulls and doorknobs.
The world's most widely consumed psychoactive substance works by mimicking adenosine's shape and blocking its receptors, keeping you awake — what is this stimulant?

This German-Swedish pharmacist had a knack for discovery — molybdenum, tungsten, barium, chlorine, and arguably oxygen all trace to his bench — but the same hands-on chemistry may have killed him via mercury poisoning. Which unlucky genius is it?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele: Swedish German chemist who discovered oxygen (1742–1786)
Descended from land mammals but now fully aquatic, this group swims via up-and-down tail strokes and includes toothed members capable of echolocation — what group includes whales and dolphins?
Known for an exceptionally loud song produced by rapid buckling of drum-like tymbals, some periodical members of this insect superfamily emerge en masse only every 13 or 17 years — which insect?
Cicada: Superfamily of insects. The cicadas are a superfamily, the Cicadoidea, of insects in the order Hemiptera (true bugs).
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
This mostly inactive steroid hormone is created when an enzyme shields organs like the kidneys by converting active cortisol into its inactive form — what is it?
Cortisone: Corticosteroid precursor and metabolite of cortisol.
Started in 1955 by an army colonel and a cynologist as an experiment, this hybrid dog breed became officially recognized as a national breed in 1982 — which one?
Czechoslovakian Wolfdog: Czech and Slovak breed of dog.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a single day, this condition is most often caused by an intestinal infection from contaminated food or water — what is it?

Diarrhea: Loose or liquid bowel movements. Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
Smaller and shorter-necked than their swan and goose cousins in the family Anatidae, these aquatic birds are often confused with grebes, loons, and coots — what are they?
Duck: Common name for many species of bird.
Co-founding Mattel with his wife Ruth, this inventor helped bring Barbie, Hot Wheels, and Chatty Cathy to toy shelves — who is he?
Elliot Handler: American inventor and business magnate (1916–2011)
Made by yeast fermenting sugars and once used as a general anesthetic, this colorless flammable liquid is the world's second most consumed drug, behind only caffeine — what is it?
Proposed in 1724 by a physicist who set water's freezing point at 32 degrees and boiling at 212, this temperature scale was originally anchored to a freezing brine solution — which scale?
Fahrenheit: Temperature scale. The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale based on one proposed in 1724 by the physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit (1686–1736).
Grown for both food and fiber, this plant's seeds are pressed into linseed oil while its stem fibers are woven into linen for sheets and clothing. What plant is it?
This Canadian physician and author has written five books linking childhood trauma to conditions like ADHD and addiction, though critics question the evidence behind some claims — who is he?
Caused by a genetic variant in the UGT1A1 gene, this harmless liver condition slows the breakdown of bilirubin and can trigger jaundice during stress, exercise, or fasting — what is it called?
Gilbert's syndrome: Medical condition. It is typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and occasionally in an autosomal dominant pattern depending on the type of variant.

Despite its name, this marine reptile's shell ranges from olive to black — its nickname actually comes from the color of the fat beneath its carapace, built up from an all-plant diet — which species is this?
Green sea turtle: Species of large sea reptile. The dorsoventrally flattened body of C. mydas is covered by a large, teardrop-shaped carapace; it has a pair of large, paddle-like flippers.

Made by fusing heavy nuclei in tiny quantities, this superheavy element 108 has a special isotope whose "magic numbers" of protons and neutrons make its deformed nucleus unusually stable — what is it?
Hassium: Chemical element with atomic number 108 (Hs)
Its name means 'river horse' in Ancient Greek, yet this semiaquatic sub-Saharan giant — the largest even-toed ungulate alive — is more closely tied to pigs than to horses; what is it?
Hippopotamus: Species of large semi-aquatic mammal.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.

This Dutch microscopist showed that an insect's egg, larva, pupa, and adult are all one animal, pioneered the microscope in dissections, and in 1658 became the first to observe red blood cells — who was he?
Jan Swammerdam: Dutch biologist and microscopist (1637–1680)
Committed to accuracy and verification, this occupation and set of methods involves gathering and distributing the day's news — what field is it?
Journalism: Production of reports on current events.
Native to southern China and roughly the size of a large olive, which citrus fruit closely resembles a tiny orange and is famously cold-hardy?
Kumquat: Species of small fruit-bearing tree.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Males of this widespread dabbling duck species sport iridescent green heads, while females have brown-speckled plumage — which bird?
Mallard: Species of duck. The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
An oily alkaloid from nightshade plants like tobacco, it doubles as a potent insect neurotoxin and once served as an insecticide, inspiring the neonicotinoid pesticides — what is it?
Nicotine: Chemical stimulant produced by some plants.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.

Detected by receptors in your muscles, tendons, and joints, this sense tells your brain where your body is in space, working alongside vision and balance to keep you upright and coordinated — what's it called?
Proprioception: Sense of self-movement, force, and body position.
Found in notable amounts in capers, red onions, and kale, this bitter-tasting plant flavonol is a popular ingredient in dietary supplements — what compound?
Quercetin: Chemical compound. It is found in many fruits, vegetables, leaves, seeds, and grains; capers, red onions, and kale are common foods containing appreciable amounts of it.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Caused by the same Group A strep behind strep throat, this childhood illness brings a sandpapery red rash and a bumpy tongue — what is it?
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.
For 30 years this English theoretical astrophysicist held Cambridge's most prestigious academic post—the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. Who?
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
A British-American structural biologist who shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for revealing the structure of the ribosome, he later served as President of the Royal Society — who is he?
Once nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse,' this British sighthound is believed to have the fastest idle-to-running acceleration of any dog breed — which breed?
Whippet: British breed of dog. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this strategist was sought out three times by Liu Bei and helped engineer victory at the Battle of Red Cliffs — who is he?
Zhuge Liang: Chinese statesman and strategist (181–234)

What is the chemical symbol for gallium?
The symbol for gallium is Ga. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Audrey Hepburn: Audrey Kathleen Hepburn (née Ruston; 4 May 1929 – 20 January 1993) was a British actress and humanitarian.

Trainspotting (film): Based on the 1993 novel by Irvine Welsh, the film was released in the United Kingdom on 23 February 1996.
